title: Sit with what you already know
subtitle: A quieter dialogue with the steadier, deeper part of you.

steps.body:
This is a quieter practice.

You're not meeting a wounded part now, but a part of you that already knows something — call it a deeper steadiness, an inner ground. It speaks best when you're reasonably settled. Whatever comes will be yours, not a voice from outside.

steps.title: How settled do you feel, coming in?
steps.body: An honest read. There's no wrong answer.

There's some charge here, and this practice asks for a steady base. You might settle first — the grounding practice is on the home screen — and come back. Or, if you feel steady enough, keep going. Your call.
Take a few slow breaths. Let yourself settle into the present, into your body, into the chair.

steps.title: Is there an image for this deeper knowing in you?
steps.body: A figure, a presence, a place, a steadiness. What would you call it?
steps.placeholder: A still figure, a light, a quiet voice, a wide place…

steps.title: What does it look or feel like?

steps.speaker: part
steps.prompt: Let this part speak. What does it want you to know right now? Write as it.
steps.hint: Let it surprise you — this isn't the advice you'd reach for on your own.

steps.speaker: you
steps.prompt: What do you want to ask it?

steps.speaker: part
steps.prompt: Let it answer, in its own words.

steps.body: Sit with that for a moment. Let it land.

steps.speaker: you
steps.prompt: Anything you want to say back?

steps.speaker: part
steps.prompt: Let it offer one last thing before you go.

steps.title: What, of what this part knows, do you want to carry with you?

exit.body: Whatever came, it came from you. That knowing was yours all along — you just made room to hear it.
